scenes.heading: When to bring on additional help as your client roster grows

sents.d: When to bring on additional help as your client roster grows
Taking on more accounts than you can manage well hurts every client, not just the newest one.

Consistently missed messages, delayed content posting, or declining quality across your roster are signals you're managing more accounts than you can handle well — addressing this before a creator notices protects both the relationships and your reputation.

Bringing on additional help (a assistant handling scheduling or first-pass messaging, under your oversight) lets you take on more roster without quality slipping, but requires the same clear boundaries documentation you'd want for yourself.

It's reasonable, and often necessary, to pause taking on new creators once you're at capacity rather than stretching thin across too many accounts — a smaller, well-managed roster builds a better reputation than a large, inconsistently managed one.

take: Add help or pause new clients before quality slips.
